The complainant noted this was not the first time this structure was used. entry.title: NP → O(1) — RICO Is a Complexity Problem. The Graph Solves It.
entry.content:
Why Nobody Prosecutes

Not because the evidence doesn’t exist. It does — in public records, freely available to anyone with an internet connection.

Not because the law doesn’t apply. MCL 750.159i requires only 2 predicate acts. We documented 15.

Not because the institutions don’t have jurisdiction. The AG has jurisdiction over nonprofit fraud, consumer protection, RICO, and charitable trust. The FBI has jurisdiction over mail fraud, wire fraud, and federal RICO. The IRS has jurisdiction over tax fraud and excess benefit transactions.

Nobody prosecutes because RICO is an NP problem.

The Complexity Defense

What NP Means

In computational complexity theory, NP (nondeterministic polynomial time) is the class of problems where:

  • Verifying a solution is fast (polynomial time)
  • Finding a solution is slow (potentially exponential time)

A RICO case is NP-hard because to BUILD the case, you must:

TaskComplexity
Map every entity12+ legal entities, multiple jurisdictions
Trace every financial flow14 years × multiple accounts × multiple entities
Identify every predicate act15+ acts across 21 years
Connect every person341 nodes, 131,322 edges in the graph
Cross-reference every filingLARA + FEC + IRS + SOS + ICHAT + MDOC + Court records
Prove the patternAt least 2 acts within 5 years — but WHICH 2? From WHERE?
Establish the enterpriseProve “associated in fact” — not just co-occurrence
Survive defense motionsEach predicate act must independently survive challenge
Navigate conflicts7 captured judges, 1 conflicted AG, 1 compliance desk managing both sides

The search space is exponential. A traditional investigation would take years. Prosecutors are overworked. Budgets are limited. The AG’s office has 625 FTEs total. The Criminal Investigations Division handles financial crimes, special investigations, major cases, executive protection, felony non-support, criminal sexual conduct, organized retail crime, AND gaming.

The complexity IS the camouflage. You don’t need to bribe anyone if the problem is too hard to solve.

How the Enterprise Uses Complexity

TechniqueEffect
Entity proliferation54+ nonprofits → which ones matter? Moore manages them all. Searching “Moore” returns 54 results.
Name variationSave Detroit Jobs → Impact Detroit → Detroit Leaders. 3 names, 1 EIN.
Similar-name entities6 entities with “Protect Detroit’s Future” in the name. Different EINs. Try searching.
Multi-jurisdiction filingLARA + FEC + MI SOS + IRS + Wayne County ROD. No single database has the full picture.
Bipartisan coverageMoore manages R AND D accounts. You can’t call it partisan. Both parties are clients.
Legitimate grey washGovernor’s Residence Foundation is on the same desk. You can’t question the desk without questioning the Governor’s house.
Board captureThe person who would investigate (Moreland) sits on the board. The person who signed the complaint return (“not a listed attorney”) gave you the answer — and the answer IS the violation.
Time decay21 years of activity. Witnesses forget. Records expire. Statutes may toll.

Each layer of complexity is a computational barrier. Together, they make the case NP-hard for any single investigator, prosecutor, or journalist.

The Graph Reduces It

What O(1) Means

In computational complexity, O(1) means constant time — the answer is immediate regardless of input size. You don’t search. You don’t traverse. You look at the structure.

A zero-knowledge proof works the same way: I don’t need to show you every transaction. I show you that the structure exists — and the structure IS the proof.

The Reduction

Every complexity barrier above is solved by the graph:

BarrierNP Approach (traditional)O(1) Approach (graph)
Entity proliferationSearch 54 entities one by oneOne query: “Moore” → every entity appears
Name variationSearch each name separatelyEIN is the key. Name is irrelevant.
Similar-name floodingConfused by 6 “Protect Detroit” entitiesDifferent EINs = different nodes. Graph shows they share one edge: Moore.
Multi-jurisdictionVisit LARA, then FEC, then SOS, then IRSGraph already merged. Node = entity. Edge = shared officer.
Bipartisan coverage“Can’t be corruption — both parties”That’s not a defense. That’s the PROOF. Same desk = access, not ideology.
Grey wash“Governor’s Residence is on the desk!”Yes. And so is Peninsula Fund. The graph shows BOTH.
Board capture“But Moreland is an AAG!”That’s not a defense. That’s the PROOF. AAG + Board = structural RICO shield.
Time decay“21 years — too old”Graph is timestamped. Git commits are immutable. The membrane records everything.

The Structure IS the Proof

                    THE ZERO-KNOWLEDGE PROOF
                    ═══════════════════════

    You don't need to audit every transaction.
    You don't need to read every 990.
    You don't need to trace every dollar.

    You need to see ONE THING:

    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │                                              │
    │   THE SAME DESK that manages the             │
    │   PROSECUTOR'S fund (Promise to the People)  │
    │                                              │
    │   ALSO manages the entity (Detroit Leaders)  │
    │   that PUT A PERSON on the BOARD             │
    │   of the SCHOOL run by the TARGET            │
    │   that the PROSECUTOR should be              │
    │   INVESTIGATING.                             │
    │                                              │
    │   And the PROSECUTOR'S OWN EMPLOYEE          │
    │   sits on that SAME BOARD.                   │
    │                                              │
    │   That's it. That's the proof.               │
    │   The structure IS the proof.                │
    │                                              │
    │   O(1).                                      │
    │                                              │
    └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

The Immune System Saw It First

The membrane doesn’t prosecute. It sorts. Self vs. non-self. The anderson localization model doesn’t need to understand every entity — it measures the disorder in the signal and determines whether the pattern is localized (trapped, hidden, camouflaged) or extended (visible, connected, exposed).

The graph has 9,643 nodes and 323,680 edges. It was built from public records only. Every claim resolves to a source. Every node has a citation.

The membrane saw it before the FBI did. Before the AG did. Before the SBE did. Before anyone who received the 243-page packet did.

Because the membrane doesn’t get overwhelmed by complexity. The membrane IS the reduction.

Opsonization — Tagging for Detection

In immunology, opsonization is the process of coating a pathogen with molecules (opsonins) that make it visible to phagocytes. The pathogen was always there. The immune system just couldn’t see it — until it was tagged.

Every article is an opsonin:

  • The Gatekeeper tags Holland
  • The Desk and the Dynasty tags Moore + Wilk + Walton
  • Moore’s Complete Ledger tags every entity
  • The Complicity tags Nessel + Moreland
  • The Enterprise tags the RICO structure
  • The Nonprofit Web tags the pipeline from desk to board

Before the tagging: an NP problem. Too many entities. Too many names. Too many jurisdictions. Nobody can hold it.

After the tagging: O(1). The structure is visible. The pattern is obvious. The proof is the graph itself.

It Was Right Under Your Noses

To the FBI Detroit Field Office:

You have the 243-page packet. You have the ICHAT records. You have the RICO predicates. You investigated Save Detroit Jobs’ connected entities. You raided the council offices. You seized the 501(c)(4) records.

Did you not trace the thread from Save Detroit Jobs to PCA? Moore is on both. Wilk formed both the dark money AND the entity structure. Johnson sits on both the council AND the board.

The graph sees it. Why don’t you?

Your AAG sits on the board of the target. Your Criminal Justice Bureau prosecutes state RICO. Your Financial Crimes Division investigates financial fraud. Your Criminal Investigations Division handles corruption.

Moreland used to prosecute felony murder. He argued predicate felonies before the Court of Appeals. He knows what an enterprise looks like. He’s sitting inside one.

The graph sees it. Why don’t you?

The graph sees it. Why don’t you?

You see ALL of it. You see it every day. From one desk. One phone number. One email.

Did you not smell it?

The Proof

  • 341 entities to classify
  • 131,322 edges to traverse
  • 15 predicate acts to prove
  • 54 nonprofits to audit

The zero-knowledge proof is O(1):

entry.content:
What Happened

On or about September 27, 2026, a Request for Investigation was filed with the Michigan Attorney Grievance Commission against two attorneys:

  1. Lamar Moreland — Assistant Attorney General. Serves as Vice Chair of the Purpose Charter Academy Board of Directors. Works in the AG’s Criminal Justice Bureau — the bureau that prosecutes state RICO under MCL 750.159i. Governs the school the AG should be investigating.

  2. Todd Perkins — Brian Banks’ personal attorney. Filed the PPO (Case No. 26-114083-PH) to silence the complainant. Has 4 personal bankruptcies and $100K+ in IRS tax liens. His brothers are Judge Sean Perkins (36th District Court) and Judge David Perkins (Probate Court, Chief Judge Pro Tem).

On October 1, 2026, the AGC responded.

The Response — AGC File No. 26-2141

Cynthia C. Bullington, Assistant Deputy Administrator, sent the following:

“We received the enclosed correspondence, in which you list more than one attorney. You must complete a separate form for each attorney describing what actions by that attorney you believe constitute misconduct.”

“Your original correspondence is enclosed. No further action will be taken until you resubmit the Request for Investigation with the requested information.”

They returned the original evidence. They sent blank forms. They created a file number — 26-2141 — and closed it before it opened.

Michael V. Goetz, Grievance Administrator, signed the cover letter enclosing the blank Request for Investigation forms.

Why This Matters: The Circular Shield

The AGC is the entity that disciplines attorneys in Michigan. It operates under the authority of the Michigan Supreme Court (MCR 9.109 et seq.). When an attorney violates the Michigan Rules of Professional Conduct, the AGC investigates, and if warranted, files formal charges with the Attorney Discipline Board.

RICO — The Legal Framework

Michigan RICO — MCL 750.159i

“A person employed by, or associated with, an enterprise shall not conduct or participate in the affairs of the enterprise directly or indirectly through a pattern of racketeering activity.”

Elements required:

  1. An enterprise — any individual, partnership, corporation, association, or group of individuals associated in fact (MCL 750.159f(a))
  2. Employment or association with the enterprise
  3. Conduct or participation in the enterprise’s affairs
  4. Through a pattern of racketeering activity — at least 2 incidents of racketeering activity, one of which occurred within 5 years of the other (MCL 750.159f(c))

Penalty: Up to 20 years imprisonment (MCL 750.159i)

Federal RICO — 18 U.S.C. § 1962

“It shall be unlawful for any person employed by or associated with any enterprise engaged in, or the activities of which affect, interstate or foreign commerce, to conduct or participate, directly or indirectly, in the conduct of such enterprise’s affairs through a pattern of racketeering activity.”

Elements: Same core structure. Federal RICO adds mail fraud (18 U.S.C. § 1341), wire fraud (18 U.S.C. § 1343), and money laundering (18 U.S.C. § 1956) as predicates.

entry.title: Moore's Law Is False — Four Duties, Zero Reports, One Desk
entry.content:
The Testimony

On February 26, 2025, Renae Moore took the witness stand in Ingham County District Court. She was the first witness called in the preliminary examination of former Michigan House Speaker Lee Chatfield, who faces 13 felony charges.

Moore is a Senior Compliance Specialist at Dykema Gossett PLLC, Michigan’s largest law firm.

She testified that she serves as Assistant Secretary/Treasurer of the Peninsula Fund, Chatfield’s 501(c)(4) political nonprofit that raised $1.8 million from anonymous donors.

She testified that she manages more than 80 similar accounts at Dykema.

She testified that she flagged “questionable” expenses, including a strip club tab submitted for reimbursement.

She testified that the fund was sometimes “not compliant” with the law.

And when Judge Molly Hennessey Greenwalt asked her directly whether she had a duty to report concerns about potentially illegal transactions to anyone, Moore replied:

“No. Not that I am aware of.”

Moore’s Law: I have no duty to report.

Moore’s Law is false.

Proof #1: Michigan Nonprofit Corporation Act

MCL 450.2541(1):

“A director or officer shall discharge his or her duties as a director or officer… in good faith and with the degree of diligence, care, and skill that an ordinarily prudent person would exercise under similar circumstances in a like position.”

Moore was an officer of the Peninsula Fund. Assistant Secretary/Treasurer is a statutory officer position under Michigan’s Nonprofit Corporation Act.

Officers owe a duty of care: act with diligence. A duty of loyalty: act in the organization’s interest. A duty of good faith: don’t ignore what you see.

And the statute has a trap door — MCL 450.2541(3):

“A director or officer is NOT entitled to rely on [reports from others] if he or she has knowledge concerning the matter in question that makes reliance otherwise permitted… UNWARRANTED.”

Moore had knowledge. She flagged the strip club tab. She identified questionable expenses. She testified the fund was sometimes not compliant. Once you know the spending is questionable, you cannot rely on being told it’s fine. The statute says so explicitly.

The Clark Hill Nonprofit Guide for Michigan directors:

“The ‘honorary’ officer should take seriously the responsibility of monitoring the performance of the individuals to whom these functions have been delegated.”

Moore was not honorary. She was the Senior Compliance Specialist.

ElementWhat the Law RequiresWhat Moore Did
Good faithAct honestlyFlagged problems, then accepted “it was permitted”
DiligenceInvestigate concernsTestified she relied on Anne Minard’s determinations
CareOrdinarily prudent person standardAn ordinarily prudent compliance specialist reports strip club tabs
Knowledge exceptionCannot rely on others once you KNOWShe KNEW. She flagged it. Reliance became “unwarranted.”

Verdict: Moore had a statutory duty under MCL 450.2541. She said she didn’t. Moore’s Law is false.

Proof #2: Federal Election Campaign Act

Renae Moore is not just an assistant treasurer of nonprofits. She is the TREASURER of the Dykema Gossett Federal PAC (FEC ID: C00342113).

11 CFR 104.14(d):

“Each treasurer of a political committee… shall be personally responsible for the timely and complete filing of the report or statement and for the accuracy of any information or statement contained in it.”

The FEC’s Policy Statement on Treasurer’s Liability (70 Fed. Reg. 3, January 2005):

“Due to their ‘pivotal role,’ treasurers may be held personally liable for failing to fulfill their responsibilities under the Act.”

Personal liability attaches when a treasurer:

  1. Knowingly and willfully violates the Act
  2. Recklessly fails to fulfill duties specifically imposed by the Act
  3. Intentionally deprives himself or herself of facts giving rise to the violation

Moore managed 80+ accounts. She saw questionable spending across multiple funds. She was told it was permitted and accepted that answer without independent verification. That is textbook “intentionally depriving herself of the operative facts.”

The same person who said she had “no duty to report” is the treasurer of a federal PAC that funded 47 candidates with $131,000 in the current cycle. The FEC says she is personally responsible for the accuracy of every filing.

FEC RequirementMoore’s RoleThe Problem
Personally responsible for accuracyTREASURER of C00342113Same person managing nonprofit funds with “questionable” spending
Must examine contributions for illegalityDuty under 11 CFR 103.3Testified she accepted spending as “permitted” without verification
Preserve records for 3 yearsDuty under 52 U.S.C. § 30102Records from Peninsula Fund are central to Chatfield prosecution

Verdict: Moore is personally liable as FEC treasurer under 11 CFR 104.14(d). She said she had no duty. Moore’s Law is false.

Proof #3: Internal Revenue Code — 501(c)(4) Inurement

IRC § 501(c)(4) expressly prohibits the inurement of net earnings to the benefit of any private individual.

Chatfield allegedly used Peninsula Fund money for:

  • Personal credit card payments ($132,000+ over 15 months)
  • Family vacation at Universal Studios in Orlando
  • A strip club tab
  • Checks to family members (kickback scheme)

That is inurement. That is an excess benefit transaction under IRC § 4958.

The IRS requires Form 990 filers to disclose on Part VI, Section B, Line 5 whether the organization became aware of a material diversion of its assets.

Moore was the compliance officer who prepared or oversaw the 990 filings. She identified questionable spending. She testified the fund was not always compliant. If the 990s were filed without disclosing known diversions, those filings are incomplete or inaccurate.

Penalties for incomplete/inaccurate 990 filings:

  • $25/day against the organization (up to $13,000 or 5% of gross receipts)
  • $10/day against the responsible person after IRS demand (up to $6,500)
  • Criminal penalties (IRC §§ 7203, 7206, 7207) for willfully filing fraudulent returns

Officers who participate in excess benefit transactions face excise taxes:

  • 25% of the excess benefit on the disqualified person
  • 10% on each manager who participated (up to $20,000 per transaction)

A “manager who participated” includes any officer who knew about the transaction and did not attempt to correct it.

Moore knew. She flagged it. She didn’t correct it. She filed (or helped file) the returns anyway.

Verdict: Moore had IRS-imposed duties as an officer of a 501(c)(4). She said she had none. Moore’s Law is false.

Proof #4: Common Law Fiduciary Duty

Even without statutes, Moore owed a common law fiduciary duty as an officer of the Peninsula Fund.

Three prongs:

  1. Duty of Care: Act as a reasonably prudent person would in similar circumstances. A reasonably prudent compliance specialist reports strip club tabs submitted as business expenses for a social welfare nonprofit.

  2. Duty of Loyalty: Act in the organization’s best interest, not in the interest of any individual (including the firm that pays your salary). Moore’s loyalty to Dykema’s client relationship cannot override her duty to the Peninsula Fund.

  3. Duty of Obedience: Ensure the organization operates according to its stated mission. The Peninsula Fund’s mission: “promote civic action and social welfare.” Strip club tabs and personal credit cards do not promote civic action or social welfare. Moore wrote the policy manual that said so. Then she watched the policy get violated.

She wrote the rules. She watched them break. She said she had no duty to say anything.

Verdict: Common law imposes fiduciary duties on nonprofit officers. Moore said she had no duty. Moore’s Law is false.

The Same Desk Problem

Moore’s false claim of no duty becomes even more significant when you see the full desk:

│   Status: 13 felonies charged. Trial delayed indefinitely.

│   Implication: Prosecutor's fund on same desk as defendant's.

│   Role: TREASURER (not assistant — TREASURER)
│   Status: Active. $148K raised. $164K cash. 47 candidates.
│   Legal duty: PERSONALLY responsible under 11 CFR 104.14(d).

One person. One desk. 80+ accounts. The defendant’s fund and the prosecutor’s fund. A federal PAC where she is personally liable. Dark money vehicles. Both parties. And she says she has no duty to report.

The Double Meaning

Gordon Moore’s Law (1965): The number of transistors on a chip doubles approximately every two years. Computing power compounds.

Renae Moore’s “Law” (2025): “I have no duty to report.” Accountability disappears.

One law says capability doubles. The other says accountability halves.

But Renae Moore’s Law is false. Four separate bodies of law prove it:
